Commentary.Commentary: Neil Broom made most of the platform and scored a half century. However, some disciplined bowling towards the end by Ireland, saw them pick crucial wickets at regular basis thus halting the scoring rate. Ireland will fancy their chances of chasing this target against an inexperienced Black Caps bowling line-up to register their first ODI win against them. Join us back for the chase...

Ireland have done well to restrict New Zealand below 300. After Luke Ronchi got New Zealand off to a flier in the first Powerplay, Ireland did well to pull the run rate back by taking two quick wickets. Ross Taylor and George Worker steadied the ship for New Zeland with a good 84-run partnership and setting a platform for the big-hitters.
Very full wide outside off, driven to extra cover for a single. NEW ZEALAND FINISH ON 289/7!
Full outside off, Kuggeleijn drives it stylishly but finds sweeper cover. A single is taken.
Wide yorker squeezed out on the off side for a brace.
Mitchell Santner walks out to bat.

OUT! Chase has his first! Back of a length, angling away, Neesham looks to muscle it over long off but fails to hit it cleanly. It goes straight to McCarthy at long off, who makes no mistake. Ireland are striking at regular intervals.
Full on the stumps, lofted over the bowler's head. The fielder in the deep cuts it off and keeps it down to a brace.
Banged in short, Jimmy looks to ramp it but misses.
Wide! Down the leg side, Neesham misses his flick and a wide is signalled.
Back of a length, pulled on the leg side for a brace.
A short delivery which has been pulled away. They manage to come back for the second.
FOUR! Shortish delivery, smashed over mid-wicket for a boundary.

Angling down leg, Neesham turns it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Short delivery, pulled over wide mid on for a single.
Low full toss, Broom gets low across to scoop but gets an inside edge on the leg side. A single is taken.
Outside off, pushed through covers for a single.
Broom makes room, O'Brien follows him with a short delivery. Broom does well to pull it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
On a length around off, Neesham dances down and hits it over mid off for a single.
Pitched outside off, pushed in the cover region for a single.
Kevin O'Brien to bowl his last over.
Low full toss outside off, Broom gets low and places it towards short third man for a single.

Wide! Banged in short, it's over the batsman's head and a wide is signalled.
Tim Murtagh is back on.
Angling into the pads, clipped on the leg side for a brace.
DROPPED! Short delivery, pulled over backward square leg. Simi Singh in the deep drops it down. He is having a mix day in field tonight.

The umpires and the players are out in the middle. The New Zealand skipper Tom Latham walks out with Luke Ronchi to open the batting. Tim Murtagh to start the proceedings with the ball. Two slips in place. Here we go...

Tom Latham says that they wanted to bat first only. Feels that it is a good wicket with a little grass on it. Hopes that the wicket plays well throughout. Mentions the two debutants - SCOTT KUGGELEIJN and SETH RANCE.

William Porterfield says that they are going to bowl first. Feels that it's a pretty decent surface. Mentions that they will want to take some early wickets. Informs the one change - SIMI SINGH makes his debut.
TOSS - Ireland win the toss and opt to field.

Hello and a warm welcome to the 2nd ODI of this Ireland Tri-Nation series in Dublin. The hosts were off to a good start in the first ODI before rain played the spoilsport. Their bowlers would want to replicate a similar performance against an inexperienced Kiwi side. The Black Caps are led by Tom Latham and he would hope that the youngsters in his team step up and the senior players make all their experience count.
